items.q: The six presentations of glomerular disease listed are asymptomatic, macrohematuria, nephrotic syndrome and:
opts: Nephritic syndrome, RPGN and chronic kidney disease (chronic GN)
Nephritic syndrome, renal vein thrombosis and CKD
Nephritic syndrome, RPGN and medullary sponge kidney
items.exp: Presentations: asymptomatic, macrohematuria, nephrotic syndrome, nephritic syndrome (acute GN), RPGN, CKD (chronic GN). (Book p756)

items.q: Match each pattern with its book label — 1) Nephritic syndrome 2) CKD of glomerular disease 3) CKD of vascular disease … A) Ischemic nephropathy B) CKD CGN (chronic glomerulonephritis) C) Acute glomerulonephritis
items.exp: Nephritic syndrome = acute GN; CKD of glomerular disease = CKD CGN; CKD of vascular disease = ischemic nephropathy. (Book p756)

items.q: The m/c presentation that heads the biopsy-indication flowchart is:
items.exp: Asymptomatic urine abnormalities (m/c presentation) lead to biopsy. (Book p756)

items.q: Asymptomatic urine abnormalities go to biopsy with proteinuria above 500 mg/24 hrs plus microhematuria of at least:
items.exp: Proteinuria (>500 mg/24 hrs) + microhematuria (≥3 RBC/HPF); proteinuria alone >1 g/24 hrs → biopsy. (Book p756)

items.q: Fill up: In the macrohematuria 40/5/1 rule, the "1" stands for one ______ plus significant proteinuria.
items.exp: 40/5/1 rule: ≥40 dysmorphic, ≥5 acanthocytes, 1 RBC cast + significant proteinuria → biopsy. (Book p756)

items.q: Match each number of the macrohematuria rule with its finding — 1) ≥40 2) ≥5 3) 1 … A) RBC cast B) Dysmorphic RBCs C) Acanthocytes
